definitions.explanation: Administrative suffix used for Osaka and Kyoto prefectures.

examples.japanese: {大阪|おおさか}{府|ふ}に{住|す}んでいる。
{京都|きょうと}{府|ふ}は{歴史|れきし}ある{場所|ばしょ}だ。
examples.english: Kyoto Prefecture is a place with history.

examples.japanese: {府|ふ}と{県|けん}の{違|ちが}いは{歴史的|れきしてき}なものだ。
examples.english: The difference between fu and ken is historical.

notes:
{府|ふ} is an administrative designation for urban prefectures in Japan.

USAGE:
Only two prefectures use {府|ふ}:
- {大阪|おおさか}{府|ふ} (Osaka)
- {京都|きょうと}{府|ふ} (Kyoto)

JAPANESE PREFECTURAL DIVISIONS:
- {都|と}: Tokyo only ({東京都|とうきょうと})
- {道|どう}: Hokkaido only ({北海道|ほっかいどう})
- {府|ふ}: Osaka, Kyoto
- {県|けん}: All other 43 prefectures

ETYMOLOGY:
The {府|ふ} designation dates from the Meiji period when these cities served as major urban centers. There were originally more {府|ふ} designations, but most were changed to {県|けん}.

RELATED WORDS:
- {県|けん}: prefecture (most common)
- {知事|ちじ}: prefectural governor
- {府民|ふみん}: residents of Osaka/Kyoto Prefecture
